payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_suite.py::test_cellspecs_renames_comment_names_both_its_readers stayed green with the criterion's own edit applied to saffron/gates/suite.py. The claim was '`saffron/cell/session.py:375-376`\'s comment above `CellSpec.renames` reads "`intake.Spec.renames`, read by `census_gate` through the suite\'s `SuiteSpec` protocol (`SA-0387`). Empty where the spec declares none." It names one consumer. `SA-0389` (`e2b2a0b0`) gave `GateSuite._run` a second: `revert_gate`, handed `spec.renames` at `saffron/gates/suite.py:202`, the same keyword `census_gate` is handed at `saffron/gates/suite.py:234`. Rewrite the comment to name both gates by their literal names, still citing `SA-0387`, and now `SA-0389` too. Change no other line of the class. The witness reads `saffron/cell/session.py`\'s own source at import time, finds the line assigning `renames: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)`, and walks backward from it collecting every contiguous line immediately above that starts with `#`. It asserts the literal substrings `census_gate` and `revert_gate` both sit inside that collected run. A comment that drops either name, that names neither by a vaguer phrase, that is deleted outright, or that sits somewhere else in the file instead of directly above the field, fails one of the two assertions or leaves the collected run empty.'. Under the edit the whole `tests` gate failed tests/test_suite.py::test_the_suite_hands_revert_the_specs_own_renames, and the criterion's witness did not fail.
